name: Appam with Veg Stew

ingredients.name: Raw rice (sona masoori, ponni or idli rice)
Water, for grinding
ingredients.householdMeasure: about ⅓ cup + 1 tbsp, added little by little

ingredients.name: Coconut oil, for greasing the pan
Coconut oil
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 tsp (¾ tsp to cook + ¼ tsp to finish)

ingredients.name: Ginger (adrak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1.5 cm piece, cut into thin strips

ingredients.name: Potato
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small potato, in 1.5 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½ small carrot, in 1.5 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Coconut milk (thick, packet/canned or first press)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 40 ml (about 2½ tbsp) to finish + 30 ml for the thin milk

equipment: Appam pan (appachatti), a small deep curved pan with a lid, about 20 cm
A lid that fits the appam pan (any plate or lid works)
A heavy-bottomed saucepan or small kadai with lid for the stew (or a pressure cooker: one whistle for the vegetables)
A bowl at least 3 times the batter volume for fermenting (the batter rises), covered with a plate or cloth
Ladle (about ¼ cup / 60 ml), flat spatula, spoon
Knife, chopping board, measuring cups and spoons (a teacup and teaspoons are fine stand-ins)

steps.title: Measure the rice
steps.text: Put 60 g (⅓ cup) raw rice in a bowl.
steps.visualCue: A small heap of white grains.
steps.videoShot: Rice poured from a cup into a steel bowl.

steps.title: Wash
steps.text: Cover with water, rub the rice between your palms, pour the water off. Repeat 2 more times.
steps.visualCue: The last rinse water is almost clear.
steps.cameraCheck: The washed rice in clear water
steps.videoShot: Hands swirling the rice in water.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Cover with about 3 cm of fresh water and leave it.
steps.tip: Under-soaked rice makes a gritty batter and thick, heavy appam.
steps.visualCue: The grains turn opaque white and break easily when pressed with a fingernail.
steps.cameraCheck: A soaked grain pressed between your fingers
steps.videoShot: A grain snapping softly between thumb and nail.

steps.title: Drain
steps.text: Drain the rice and discard the soaking water.
steps.visualCue: Wet, swollen grains in the sieve.
steps.videoShot: Water streaming out of the sieve.

steps.title: Load the jar
steps.text: Put the soaked rice, 15 g (1 heaped tbsp) cooked rice, 15 g (2 tbsp) grated coconut, 5 g (1 tsp) sugar and 0.5 g (a small pinch) instant yeast in the small mixer jar.
steps.tip: Cooked rice (or a little poha, as some recipes use) is what makes the appam centre soft and spongy.
steps.visualCue: Rice with coconut, cooked rice and a few yeast granules on top.
steps.videoShot: The pinch of yeast dropped into the jar.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Add 60 ml water and grind in short bursts, scraping down once, then add the remaining 30 ml little by little and grind until very smooth.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, pourable white batter; rubbed between your fingers it feels silky, not grainy.
steps.cameraCheck: A drop of batter rubbed between finger and thumb
steps.videoShot: The batter swirling in the jar.

steps.title: Check the consistency
steps.text: Pour the batter into a large bowl. It should be thinner than dosa batter, like thick buttermilk, flowing freely off the ladle.
steps.tip: Too thick and the appam will not spread up the sides of the pan; too thin and the centre stays flat and wet.
steps.visualCue: A smooth ribbon that disappears into the surface at once; about 190 g (a little under 1 cup) of batter.
steps.videoShot: The white ribbon falling back into the bowl.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Cover the bowl loosely and leave it in a warm spot. Do not add salt yet.
steps.tip: If the batter has not risen, put the bowl in a switched-off oven with the light on for 1–2 h.
steps.visualCue: The batter has risen to about double, the top is full of bubbles and it smells pleasantly yeasty and slightly sour.
steps.videoShot: A spoon dipped into the batter showing an airy, bubbly texture.

steps.title: Add salt
steps.text: Stir in 0.6 g (a pinch) salt gently, without beating out all the air. If the batter has thickened, add 1–2 tbsp water.
steps.visualCue: Still bubbly and pourable.
steps.videoShot: The spoon folding salt into the batter.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.text: Slice 40 g onion (½ small onion) thinly.
steps.visualCue: Thin half-moon slices.
steps.cameraCheck: The sliced onion on the board
steps.videoShot: A knife slicing onion.

steps.title: Prepare the aromatics
steps.text: Cut 4 g ginger into thin strips, slit 1–2 green chillies (4 g) lengthwise and pick 8–10 curry leaves.
steps.visualCue: Three small heaps: ginger strips, slit chillies, curry leaves.
steps.videoShot: Ginger cut into matchsticks.

steps.title: Cut the potato and carrot
steps.text: Peel and cut 60 g potato and 40 g carrot into 1.5 cm cubes.
steps.tip: Keep the potato cubes in water until you use them so they do not darken.
steps.visualCue: Even cubes, about the size of a sugar cube.
steps.videoShot: Carrot cubes falling off the knife.

steps.title: Cut the beans and measure the peas
steps.text: Cut 30 g French beans into 2 cm pieces and measure 20 g (2 tbsp) green peas.
steps.visualCue: Short green beans and a small heap of peas.
steps.videoShot: Beans cut on the board.

steps.title: Make the thin coconut milk
steps.text: Mix 30 ml thick coconut milk with 70 ml water in a cup. Keep 40 ml thick coconut milk aside separately.
steps.visualCue: One cup of watery thin milk, one small cup of thick creamy milk.
steps.cameraCheck: The two cups side by side
steps.videoShot: Coconut milk stirred into water.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Heat ¾ tsp (about 4 g) coconut oil in the saucepan on medium.
steps.visualCue: The oil is thin and shimmering, and smells of coconut.
steps.videoShot: Oil spreading across the hot pan.

steps.title: Fry the whole spices
steps.text: Add the cinnamon, 2 cloves, 2 crushed cardamom pods and 6–8 peppercorns.
steps.visualCue: The spices sizzle and puff slightly, with a warm, sweet smell; not darkened.
steps.videoShot: Cardamom pods sizzling.

steps.title: Add the aromatics
steps.text: Add the ginger, green chillies and curry leaves and stir.
steps.visualCue: The curry leaves crackle and turn glossy.
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with ginger and curry leaves
steps.videoShot: Curry leaves spluttering.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Add the sliced onion and cook, stirring, without browning it.
steps.tip: Kerala stew should stay creamy white, so keep the heat medium and do not brown the onion.
steps.visualCue: The onion is soft and translucent but still pale; no brown edges.
steps.videoShot: The spatula turning translucent onion.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the potato, carrot and beans and stir for 1 minute.
steps.visualCue: The vegetables are coated in oil and spices.
steps.videoShot: Vegetables tossed with the onion.

steps.title: Add the thin milk and salt
steps.text: Pour in the 100 ml thin coconut milk, add 1.0 g (a scant ¼ tsp) salt and stir.
steps.visualCue: The vegetables are just covered with milky liquid.
steps.videoShot: Thin coconut milk poured over the vegetables.

steps.title: Simmer covered
steps.text: Cover and simmer on low-medium until the vegetables are tender. Add the peas for the last 3 minutes.
steps.tip: If it gets too dry, add 2–3 tbsp water. Mash 2–3 potato cubes against the side of the pan if you like a slightly thicker stew.
steps.visualCue: A knife slides easily through a potato cube; the beans are tender but still green.
steps.cameraCheck: A potato cube pierced with a knife
steps.videoShot: The lid lifted to show the gently bubbling stew.

steps.title: Finish with thick milk
steps.text: Lower the heat, pour in the 40 ml thick coconut milk and stir gently. Heat until just steaming, then switch off.
steps.tip: Do not boil after adding the thick milk, or it can split and turn oily.
steps.visualCue: The stew is creamy white and steaming, with tiny bubbles at the edge only.
steps.videoShot: Thick coconut milk swirling into the stew.

steps.title: Finish the stew
steps.text: Drizzle ¼ tsp (about 1 g) coconut oil on top, add 2–3 fresh curry leaves (optional) and cover. Keep aside.
steps.visualCue: A thin, glossy sheen on top and a strong coconut smell.
steps.cameraCheck: The covered pan, then the open stew
steps.videoShot: Oil drizzled over the stew.

steps.title: Heat the appam pan
steps.text: Heat the appachatti on medium for about 2 minutes.
steps.visualCue: A few drops of water sprinkled in sizzle and vanish in 2–3 seconds.
steps.videoShot: Water drops dancing in the curved pan.

steps.title: Grease the pan
steps.text: Wipe a few drops of coconut oil (about ⅙ of the 2 g) over the pan with a paper towel.
steps.visualCue: A thin, even sheen, no pools of oil.
steps.videoShot: A paper towel wiping the curved surface.

steps.title: Pour and swirl
steps.text: Pour one ladle (about 60 g, ¼ cup) of batter into the centre. At once, lift the pan by both handles and swirl it in a full circle so the batter coats the sides in a thin layer, leaving the thick part in the centre.
steps.tip: Swirl only once and quickly; the batter sets on the hot sides within seconds.
steps.visualCue: A thin ring of batter up the sides and a thicker pool in the middle.
steps.cameraCheck: The swirled batter in the pan
steps.videoShot: The pan rotated in one smooth circle.

steps.title: Cover and cook
steps.text: Put the pan back on medium-low heat, cover it and cook. Do not flip.
steps.tip: A wet centre means it needs 30–60 seconds more; a dark edge means the heat is too high.
steps.visualCue: The edges turn golden and crisp and pull away from the pan; the centre is fluffy, full of small holes and no longer wet when touched lightly.
steps.cameraCheck: The lid lifted to show the cooked appam
steps.videoShot: The lid lifted, steam rising, lacy golden edge.

steps.title: Lift out
steps.text: Loosen the edge with a spatula and lift the appam out onto a plate.
steps.visualCue: A bowl-shaped appam with a crisp lacy rim and a soft white centre.
steps.videoShot: The appam sliding out of the pan.

steps.title: Make the next two appam
steps.text: Grease the pan lightly and repeat steps 26–28 twice with the rest of the batter.
steps.visualCue: Three appam, each with a lacy rim and spongy centre (the later ones are usually better than the first).
steps.videoShot: The three appam stacked side by side.

steps.title: Reheat and serve
steps.text: Warm the stew for 1 minute on low if it has cooled (do not boil) and serve it in a bowl next to the appam.
steps.visualCue: Steaming white stew with orange carrot and green beans and peas; soft, warm appam.
steps.cameraCheck: The full plate: 3 appam and a bowl of stew
steps.videoShot: A piece of appam torn and dipped into the stew.

reasons: the appam is steamed-and-griddled with very little oil and is fermented, and the stew carries about 190 g of vegetables, giving about 9.5 g fibre, good vitamin A, potassium and vitamin K, with no cholesterol and no frying. Against it: the base is white rice (high glycaemic load), protein is low (about 11 g for 650 kcal), and coconut milk, coconut oil and grated coconut push saturated fat to about 25 g, above the daily limit in one meal; salt is moderate (about 1.7 g). Restaurant versions are often richer in thick coconut milk or finished with ghee, saltier, and the appam may contain more sugar, so they score a little lower.

researchRating.basis: appam with stew is one of Kerala's best-known breakfasts and a festive dish (Easter and Christmas mornings in Syrian Christian homes), covered by nearly every major Indian recipe site (Veg Recipes of India, Hebbar's Kitchen, Cooking and Me, Archana's Kitchen, Sailu's Food, Jeyashri's Kitchen, My Food Story) and widely described as a "classic" or "very popular" combination. Points off because home cooks often report flat or dense appam when fermentation fails, and one Mumbai diner review called a restaurant veg stew "sad", preferring non-veg stews. Recipe vote counts could not be checked (pages blocked).

storage: Stew: fridge 2 days in a closed box (est.), within 2 hours of cooking; reheat gently on low, stirring, without boiling (coconut milk can split); freezing is not recommended (the potato turns grainy and the coconut milk separates). Cooked appam: best fresh; fridge up to 1 day, re-steam for 1–2 minutes or warm covered on a tawa; avoid the microwave. Uncooked fermented batter: fridge 2–3 days (est.); it gets more sour each day, so add a pinch of sugar and bring it to room temperature for 30 minutes before cooking.
leftoverRemix: Appam Stew Bake (Kerala-style shepherd's pie). Mash the leftover stew vegetables lightly with a spoon, spread in a small oven dish, cover with torn leftover appam pieces brushed with a little coconut oil and a pinch of pepper, and bake or air-fry at 180 °C for 10–12 minutes until the appam turns crisp and golden. Leftover batter makes sweet coconut pancakes: stir in 1 tbsp jaggery and a pinch of cardamom and cook small thick rounds on a tawa.
burnOff: about 9.3 km of running (650 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 13 km of brisk walking (about 2 h 35 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.).

navratri.reason: the appam is made of rice, which is avoided on the common North and West Indian vrat rule set, and the stew has onion

ekadashi.reason: rice is the main food given up on the common Ekadashi rule set

jain.reason: drop the potato, carrot, onion and fresh ginger (roots and bulbs) and use beans, peas, cauliflower and capsicum; check family practice on overnight-fermented batter

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so there is no halal concern; soft, mild and easy to digest for iftar; moderate salt (about 1.6 g), but rich in coconut fat, so keep the portion moderate at sehri

jain.reason: drop the potato, carrot, onion and fresh ginger (all roots or bulbs) from the stew and use beans, peas, cauliflower and capsicum instead; a pinch of dry ginger powder (sonth) is allowed; many strict Jain households also avoid batter fermented overnight, so check family practice

vegan.reason: rice, coconut, coconut milk, vegetables, yeast, sugar and coconut oil; no dairy, ghee, honey or egg

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, fish or egg, so it fits a pescatarian diet

sattvik.reason: leave out the onion in the stew (no garlic is used); ginger, chilli, whole spices and curry leaves stay

glutenFree.reason: rice, coconut and vegetables only; no wheat, rava, maida or hing (some stews add a pinch of hing, which in India is usually compounded with wheat flour, so it is left out)

dairyFree.reason: coconut milk and coconut oil, no milk, curd, butter or ghee
